source_text.body:
Hand routine browser tasks to Grok Bot
A user has Grok Bot use the computer for browser tasks that can't be done directly; it handled routine ones for weeks before later refusing some.
·
Nov 8, 2026
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
The poster used Grok Bot’s computer function to handle browser work for funnel-building and automations when the GoHighLevel connection could not perform those actions. They say Grok had completed the same task about 50 times, but after a reconnect prompt it now insisted the connection did not permit it and refused to switch to the computer route; comments report similar failures on browser tasks like Figma work, job submissions, X post scheduling, and marking workflow steps complete.
How it went
For weeks it reportedly handled routine browser jobs, then a recent change made it more restrictive and blocked some previously working workflows. Commenters describe bots refusing tasks, wasting usage, and in one case losing files after a computer reset, but no fix is given.
Worth knowing
The main catch is instability: several commenters say behavior changed within the prior 12–24 hours or few days, so a workflow that works now may suddenly stop.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
Use your computer's browser to do this routine task for me: [describe task, e.g., download the monthly report from site X and save it to a folder]. Repeat it [daily/weekly] and tell me when each run finishes with a short summary of what you did. Pause and show me what you're about to do before submitting any form, making a payment, sending a message, or deleting anything.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GrokBot/comments/1xpw1ss/grok_bot_officially_killed_itself
